8101.full: 1. to leave besides as a legacy , ἀρχήν τινι (Thucydides) 2. to lose besides , τὰ αὑτῶν (Thucydides) (ML)

8102.full: to set on fire or burn besides :—;Pass., σκεύη προσκεκαυμένα pots burnt at the fire , (Aristophanes Comicus): metaphorically, προσκαίεσθαί τινι to be in love with . . , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

s: to make the scale incline one way or another; hence, metaphorically, of persons, to incline towards
8103.full: προσ-κλίνω [in LXX: 2Ma.14:24 * ;] __1. to make to lean against. __2. to make the scale incline one way or another; hence, metaphorically, of persons, to incline (sc. ἑαυτόν) towards: pass., Act.5:36.† (AS)

8108.g: painted scenery at the back of the stage
8108.full: painted scenery at the back of the stage

8109.full: προσ-λαλέω, -ῶ [in LXX: Exo.4:16 AB2 (דָבַר pi.), Wis.13:17 * ;] to speak to: Act.28:20; with dative of person(s), Act.13:43.† (AS)

8115.full: to call by a name , πρ. θεούς to give them the name θεοί, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

8120.full: to sprinkle on one, τινί τι (Strabo Geographus) (ML)

s: upper part of anything: a bust
8133.full: 1. the foremost or upper part of anything: a bust or half-figure , [variant datesAnthology Palantina 2. the forepart of a ship, [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

8134.full: προ-τάσσω [in LXX: 2Ma.8:36 R (Α, προστ-) * ;] __1. to place in front. __2. to arrange beforehand: Act.17:26, Rec. (for προστ., Edd.).† (AS)

8139.full: 1. shewing itself or seen beforehand , (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. seen clearly or plainly, conspicuous , (Xenophon Historicus) 3. metaphorically quite plain or clear , (Plato Philosophus); ἀπὸ or ἐκ τοῦ προφανοῦς openly , (Thucydides):—;adverb -νῶς, (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

s: to be on guard, keep watch
to guard oneself, to be on one's guard, take precautions
8140.full: to keep guard before, to guard a place or house, with accusative, (Homeric Hymns) (in the epic 2nd plural imperative προφύλαχθε, for προφυλάσσετε); (Xenophon Historicus); προφυλάσσειν ἐπί τινι to keep guard over a person or place, (Herdotus Historicus):—;absolute to be on guard, keep watch , ἡ προφυλάσσουσα (i.e. ναῦς); = προφυλακίς, (Herdotus Historicus): —;Mid. to guard oneself, to be on one's guard, take precautions , (Herdotus Historicus):—;with accusative to be on one's guard or take precautions against , Lat. cavere, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

8143.full: προ-ϋπ-άρχω [in LXX: Job 42:18* ;] __1. to be beforehand in. __2. to be before or previously: with ptcp., Luk.23:12, Act.8:9.† (AS)

8144.full: 1. to have gone before, be the first , (Thucydides) 2. to have advanced , πρ. ἐς βαθὺ τῆς ἡλικίας (Aristophanes Comicus); εἰς τοῦτο προήκειν to have come to this pass, (Demosthenes Orator); of Time, τῆς ἡμέρας προηκούσας (Plutarch) 3. to reach beyond , τῆς ἄρκυος (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

8148.full: πρωτο-κλυτία, -ας, ἡ the chief place at table (see Swete, Mk., l.with): Mat.23:6, Mrk.12:39, Luk.14:7-8 20:46.† (AS)

8151.full: πρωτοστάτης, -ου, ὁ (πρῶτος, ἵστημι) [in LXX: Job.15:24 AB * ;] prop., of soldiers, one who stands first, one in the front rank (Thuc., Xen.); hence, metaphorically, a leader: Act.24:5.† (AS)

8152.g: to give a right of first-born
8152.full: to give a right of first-born

s: In Athens, one who exacts payment, a collector; hence, generally , a court officer
8155.full: πράκτωρ, -ορος, ὁ (πράσσω), [in LXX: Isa.3:12 (נָגַשׁ) * ;] __1. (poët.) one who does or accomplishes. __2. In Athens, one who exacts payment, a collector; hence, generally (frequently in π., see Deiss., BS, 154), a court officer: Luk.12:58.† (AS)

8161.full: 1. a putting to, application of ladders to a wall, (Thucydides); of the cupping-glass, (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. an adding, addition , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

8163.full: 1. at hand, ready , (Aeschulus Tragicus); of a drawn sword or knife, (Sophocles Tragicus); λίθοις καὶ . . ἀκοντίοις, ὡς ἕκαστός τι πρόχειρον εἶχε (Thucydides); ὃ προχειρότατον ἔχω εἰπεῖν (Demosthenes Orator) 2. πρόχειρόν [ ἐστι] it is easy , with infinitive, (Plato Philosophus), etc. 3. of persons, ready to do, with infinitive, (Sophocles Tragicus); with dative, πρ. τῇ φυγῇ ready for flight, (Euripides) 4. adverb -ρως, off-hand, readily , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

8164.full: 1. a prince, ruler, lord, chief , of Hiero, (Pindar); of Zeus, (Pindar) 2. at Athens, a Prytanis or President : the πρυτάνεις were a committee of 50, chosen by lot from each of the 10 φυλαί, so that each set formed 1/10 part of the βουλή or Council of 500; out of these 50 πρυτάνεις one was chosen by lot as chief-president ἐπιστάτης); he chose 9 πρόεδρο; and the real business was in the hands of this smaller body, with a secretary γραμματεύς); added.—;The φυλή which first entered office every year was determined by lot; and their term of office πρυτανεία); was about five weeks. During this time all treaties and public acts ran in their name, in this form: Ἀκαμαντὶς φυλὴ, ἐπρυτάνευε, Φαίνιππος ἐγραμμάτευε, Νικιάδης ἐπεστάτει the Tribe Acamantis were the Presidency, Phaenippus the Secretary, Niciades the Chief-president, (Thucydides) (ML)

8165.full: 1. lately, just now , Lat. nuper, (Iliad by Homer), etc. 2. the day before yesterday , οὐ χθές, ἀλλὰ πρ. (Thucydides); πρώην τε καὶ χθές till yesterday or the day before , i. e. till very lately , (Herdotus Historicus); so, χθές τε καὶ πρώην (Aristophanes Comicus); πρώην καὶ χθές (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

8168.full: 1. a stumble, trip, false step , (Theognis Elegiacus) 2. a failure, misfortune, defeat , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. from πτάξ (ML)

8176.full: πυρετός, -οῦ, ὁ (πῦρ) [in LXX: Deu.28:22 (קַדַּחַת) * ;] a fever: Mat.8:15, Mrk.1:31, Luk.4:39, Jhn.4:52, Act.28:8; π. μέγας, a high fever: Luk.4:38 (on the technical phrase here, see MM, xxii).† (AS)

8177.full: giving forth fire:—; τὰ πυροβόλα bolts or arrows tipped with fire , (Plutarch) (ML)

s: the priest who kept the sacrificial fire
8180.full: 1. fire-bearing , (Aeschulus Tragicus); of lightning, (Pindar):—; πυρφόροι ὀϊστοί arrows with combustibles tied to them , (Thucydides) 2. in special senses, 3. epithet of Zeus in reference to his lightnings, (Sophocles Tragicus); of Demeter, in reference to the torches used by her worshippers, (Euripides); of Artemis, (Sophocles Tragicus); but θεὸς πυρφόρος the fire-bearing god, the god who produces plague or fever , (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. ὁ πυρφόρος, in the Lacedaemonian army, was the priest who kept the sacrificial fire , which was never allowed to go out, (Xenophon Historicus); hence proverbial of a total defeat, ἔδεε δὲ μηδὲ πυρφόρον περιγενέσθαι (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

8183.lxx: in LXX: Job.17:7 B(כָּהָה), Pro.10:20 A *
8183.full: πωρόω, -ῶ (πῶρος, 1. a stone. 2. a callus) [in LXX: Job.17:7 B(כָּהָה), Pro.10:20 A * ;] to petrify, harden, form a callus. Metaphorical, π. τ. καρδίαν, Jhn.12:40. Pass., Rom.11:7; τ. νοήματα, 2Co.3:14; ἡ καρδία, Mrk.6:52 8:17 † (AS)

8189.full: 1. near, hard by, close , with genitive, (Odyssey by Homer) 3. absolute, χριμφθεὶς πέλας (Odyssey by Homer); π. στείχειν, παρεῖναι, στῆναι [variant datesTragica Adespota 4. οἱ πέλας (i.e. ὄντες); one's neighbours , (Thucydides), etc.: hence one's fellow-creatures, all men , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

8192.full: 1. of fruit, cooked by the sun, ripe, mellow , Lat. mitis, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 2. metaphorically in vocative, mostly as a term of endearment, kind, gentle , ὦ πέπον my good friend , (Iliad by Homer); κριὲ πέπον my pet ram, (Odyssey by Homer);—; in bad sense, soft, weak , (Iliad by Homer); ὦ πέπονες ye weaklings , (Iliad by Homer): —; μόχθος πέπων softened pain, (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.: with dative, ἐχθροῖς π. gentle to one's foes, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

8193.full: a perch for fowls to roost at night, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) derivation uncertain (ML)

8195.full: an ape, monkey , (Aristophanes Comicus); as feminine, πίθηκος μήτηρ (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor):—;of persons, an ape, jackanapes , (Aristophanes Comicus) derivation uncertain (ML)

8196.full: πιθός, see: πειθός. πειθός (πιθός, WH), -ή, -όν (πείθω), = cl. πιθανός, persuasive: 1Co.2:4 (not found elsewhere).† (AS)

8197.full: 1. grass, herb , (Homer), etc.; ποία Μηδική, Lat. herba Medica, sainfoin or lucerne , (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. the grass , i. e. a grassy place , plat., (Xenophon Historicus) 3. in Poets, of Time, τέσσαρας πόας four grasses , i. e. summers , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

8199.lxx: in LXX: Da, LXX TH Dan.1:10 (מִשְׁתֶּה) *
8199.full: πόσις, -εως, ἡ (πίνω), [in LXX: Da, LXX TH Dan.1:10 (מִשְׁתֶּה) * ;] __1. prop., drinking: Rom.14:17, Col.2:16 (see Lft.; ICC, in l). __2. = πόμα, drink: Jhn.6:55 (cf. βρῶσις).† (AS)
